🧪 Hypothetical Scenarios — Exam Unit 3

31 real exam scenarios · Applied reasoning · Organized by topic · Reveal and self-assess

📊 Self-assessment: Solved: 0/0
🌳 T6.1 — Phylogeny and classification 1 case

1. You have a tree where A and B share a node, and that node then connects to C at an older node. Who is most closely related to whom?

A and B are more closely related to each other than either is to C, because their common ancestor is more recent.
🦠 T6.2 — Domains of Life (Bacteria & Archaea) 3 cases

2. You are given a unicellular organism without a nucleus. Cell wall lacks peptidoglycan, membrane lipids have ether bonds, lives at 90°C. Bacteria or Archaea?

Archaea. The absence of peptidoglycan and the ether-linked lipids are diagnostic. Bacteria have peptidoglycan and ester-linked lipids.

3. A Gram-positive bacterium loses the ability to synthesize peptidoglycan through mutation. What happens to it?

It becomes osmotically fragile (loses its structural support), lyses easily, and stops retaining crystal violet in the stain. This is essentially the mechanism by which penicillin works (it inhibits peptidoglycan synthesis).

4. An ampicillin-sensitive bacterium is mixed with a resistant bacterium that carries the resistance gene on a plasmid. After some time, the formerly sensitive ones are also resistant. What happened?

Conjugation. The plasmid carrying the resistance gene was transferred by direct contact (pili) to the sensitive bacteria. This is why antibiotic resistance spreads so rapidly.
🦠 T6.3 — Virology and infectious agents 2 cases

5. A bacterium with an integrated prophage is exposed to UV radiation. What do you predict?

The prophage can activate, enter the lytic cycle, replicate, and lyse the bacterium. This is the lysogenic → lytic transition induced by stress (UV radiation damages DNA and triggers prophage excision).

6. An infectious agent is resistant to treatments that destroy nucleic acids (nucleases) but sensitive to treatments that destroy proteins (proteases). What type is it?

Prion. Its nature is exclusively protein-based (misfolded PrP protein). It contains no nucleic acids of its own, which is why nucleases do not affect it.
🔬 T6.4 — Eukaryotes and endosymbiotic theory 1 case

7. A new organelle is discovered in a protist: double membrane, its own circular DNA, and 70S ribosomes. What hypothesis arises about its origin?

Endosymbiotic origin, probably from a bacterium. The three lines of evidence (double membrane, circular DNA, 70S ribosomes) are the diagnostic criteria used for mitochondria and chloroplasts.
🌿 T6.5 — Plants 2 cases

8. A plant has a large, green gametophyte and a small sporophyte that grows on the gametophyte and depends on it nutritionally. What group is it?

Bryophytes (mosses, liverworts, hornworts). The dominant phase is the gametophyte; the sporophyte is dependent. In ferns and seed plants this relationship is reversed.

9. If all angiosperms disappeared, what would happen to pollinators?

Mass collapse. Most pollinators (bees, butterflies, hummingbirds, bats) depend on flowers. Gymnosperms (mostly wind-pollinated) cannot sustain these pollinators. The consequence would be cascading extinction of these animal groups.
🍄 T6.6 — Fungi 1 case

10. If mycorrhizae completely die off in a forested region, what do you predict?

Reduced phosphorus and water absorption in plants → plant stress → less growth → changes in plant community composition → cascade effects on herbivores and other trophic levels. The disruption may take years but is profound.
🦑 T6.7 — Invertebrates 2 cases

11. In an embryo, the blastopore becomes the anus. What lineage does it belong to?

Deuterostomes. This places it with echinoderms and chordates. In protostomes it is the opposite: blastopore → mouth.

12. You find a bilateral aquatic animal, segmented, with a cylindrical body and setae on each segment. What phylum?

Annelid (likely a polychaete if marine). Key: segmentation + setae (chaetae). Nematodes are cylindrical but not segmented and lack setae.
🐟 T6.8 — Chordates 3 cases

13. A swimming larva with a notochord and post-anal muscular tail becomes a sessile adult lacking those features. What group is it?

Urochordate (tunicate / sea squirt). The larva is unambiguously chordate; the adult attaches to the substrate and loses the notochord and tail. The four chordate traits are only seen in the larva.

14. If the amniote egg had never evolved, which groups would not exist today?

Reptiles, birds, and mammals (all amniotes). Vertebrates would have remained confined to near water for reproduction, like modern amphibians.

15. A mammal species loses the ability to maintain a stable body temperature. What consequences do you predict?

Reduced activity in cold climates, greater dependence on thermal environment (like reptiles), drastic changes in geographic range and behavior. Some current mammals (sloths, hibernating bears) show partial versions of this.
📈 T7.1 — Population dynamics 4 cases

16. An invasive species arrives on an island with no predators or competitors. Initially it grows exponentially (J-curve). After some time, what do you predict?

It will eventually slow down (logistic model) as it hits the carrying capacity K due to food exhaustion, space limitations, or density-dependent diseases. It can cause local ecological collapse if it exceeds K.

17. A fire kills 80% of a deer population. The following year, wolves that feed on deer also decline drastically. What factor affected each one?

Deer: density-independent factor (fire, independent of how many deer there were). Wolves: density-dependent factor (prey scarcity, which depends on the size of the deer population).

18. A species produces thousands of eggs, provides no parental care, juveniles mature in weeks, and live only a few months. What demographic strategy does it show?

r selection (r strategy): high reproductive rate, little parental investment, short life, early reproduction. Typical of bony fish, insects, frogs.

19. Can humans grow indefinitely?

No. Although technology extends K, planetary resources (arable land, fresh water, energy, CO₂ absorption capacity) are finite. Unavoidable thermodynamic and ecological limits exist.
🌐 T7.2 — Communities and succession 4 cases

20. Two bird species in the same tree eat the same seeds, at the same time, on the same branch. What do you predict in the long run?

Intense competition for an identical niche. Long-term: either one displaces the other (competitive exclusion), or they partition the resource (resource partitioning: one feeds at the treetop, the other below; one by day, the other at dawn; etc.).

21. Two squirrel species share a forest. One feeds on ground seeds, the other on canopy seeds. What evolutionary process allowed this coexistence?

Resource partitioning / possible character displacement, derived from ancestral competition. Each species occupies a slightly different niche, avoiding competitive exclusion.

22. Species A benefits from the presence of species B. Species B is not clearly affected. What type of interspecific relationship is this?

Commensalism (+ / 0). Only one species benefits; the other neither gains nor loses. Example: remoras and sharks.

23. After a fire that razes a forest but leaves the soil intact, what type of succession follows?

Secondary succession. The soil allows recovery to be faster (years to decades), beginning with annual herbs and shrubs. Primary succession starts from bare rock and is much slower.
⚡ T7.3 — Energy flow and biogeochemical cycles 4 cases

24. Why are there fewer eagles than mice in an ecosystem?

Because of the 10% Rule. Mice (primary consumers) receive ~10% of plant energy; eagles (carnivores) receive only ~10% of mouse energy. There is simply much less energy available at higher trophic levels.

25. A forest has a GPP of 5,000 g/m²/year and producers respire 2,000 g/m²/year. What is the NPP?

NPP = GPP − Respiration = 5,000 − 2,000 = 3,000 g/m²/year. NPP is the biomass available to herbivores.

26. If all decomposers disappear from an ecosystem, what happens to biogeochemical cycles?

Nutrients become trapped in dead biomass. Plants cannot access recycled N, P, C. Productivity and biomass collapse within a few years. Matter cycles, but energy can no longer flow without the degradation of organic matter.

27. A river receives a massive discharge of agricultural fertilizer. What ecological sequence do you predict?

Eutrophication: algal bloom → mass death and decomposition → drop in dissolved O₂ (hypoxia) → death of fish and invertebrates → dead zone.
🌍 T7.4 — Biosphere, biomes, and sustainability 4 cases

28. A plant species flowers two weeks earlier due to rising temperatures, but its pollinator does not advance its migration. What do you predict?

Phenological desynchronization. The plant is not efficiently pollinated → reproduction falls → population may decline. The pollinator loses its resource. This is an example of mutualism disruption caused by climate change.

29. If a savanna receives much higher and constant rainfall, toward what biome would it tend to transform?

Toward a tropical rainforest (if temperature is high) or temperate forest (if lower). More humidity allows dense trees and displaces dominant grasses.

30. At abyssal hydrothermal vents no sunlight reaches, yet dense communities exist. How is this possible?

Chemosynthesis. Bacteria use H₂S (hydrogen sulfide) released by the vents as an energy source, forming the base of the food chain. It is an ecosystem completely independent of solar energy.

31. A region decides to intensively exploit timber to generate employment. After 10 years, the forests are depleted and the economy collapses. Which dimension(s) of sustainability failed?

All three dimensions. Environmental: deforestation. Economic: strategy not viable in the long term. Social: loss of sustainable employment. Sustainability fails when any dimension is completely sacrificed for the others.

💳 How to pay and activate your plan

Payments are processed via PayPal (works from any country with a card or PayPal balance). Pro access is activated manually after confirming payment.

  1. Choose your plan in the pricing section of the landing page.
  2. Complete payment with PayPal using your card or PayPal account.
  3. Use the same email you registered with in BioMaster.
  4. Your plan activates within 24 h. We'll notify you by email when it's ready.

Problem with your payment or access? Write to Biomaster.oficial@gmail.com — we respond within 24 h.

🇨🇷 Prefer to pay with SINPE Móvil? (Costa Rica only)
  1. Send SINPE Móvil to number 8713 7782.
  2. Send the receipt to Biomaster.oficial@gmail.com indicating your BioMaster email and the chosen plan.
  3. We activate your access within 24 h.

The SINPE number is exclusively for payments, not support.

🌎 Students from anywhere in the world

BioMaster accepts PayPal payments from any country. You can pay with credit or debit card (Visa, Mastercard, Amex) even without a PayPal account.

  1. Register for free and try the platform without a card.
  2. When you're ready, choose your plan in the pricing section and pay with PayPal.
  3. Use the same email registered in BioMaster. We activate your access within 24 h.

✅ PayPal works from Costa Rica, Mexico, Colombia, Peru, Argentina, and any country. Visa, Mastercard, and Amex accepted.
